newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond rally stuck at 93.210.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond rally stuck at 93.210.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract tested 93.210 in after hours trading as the U.S. Treasury market rallied further, but once again this proved a tough barrier to breach.
*U.S. bonds were spurred on by expectations the Fed would keep policy on hold in August.
The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract tested 93.210 in after hours trading, but once again this proved a tough barrier to breach.
The contract ended SYCOM at 93.200, up from Monday's soft pit close of 93.170 and after bouncing from 93.160 session low.

The firm tone was in response to a further rally in U.S. Treasuries on return from Friday's holiday for Independence day where the 30-year bond yield dropped to around its lowest since February at one stage to 6.56 percent before closing at 6.58 percent and down four basis points from Thursday's New York close.
The U.S. rally was on expectations the Federal Reserve will keep policy on hold in August and on hopes that recent central bank selling of gold will result in the buying of U.S. Treasuries.

Meanwhile, the local rally to 3-1/2 year highs on the 10-year bond contract to 93.210 is seen in need of positive support from the short-end for the advance to continue to the next resistance at 93.250, analsyts said.
However, caution in front of this Thursday's labour force report for June, and with it possible clues on monetary policy, is keeping restraining the short end for now.
